# Baghdad 830 – Medicine & hygiene

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from eras/islamic-830-baghdad.yaml — do not edit -->

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Contagion by invisible living agents (germ theory)** [`contagion_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/contagion_theory.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Disease comes from humoral imbalance, corrupt air (waba') and God's decree. Two sayings of the Prophet pull against each other, 'there is no contagion' and 'flee from the leper as you flee from a lion', and scholars argue over how to reconcile them. Nobody proposes living agents. Local: hadith scholars such as Ahmad ibn Hanbal; court physicians Yuhanna ibn Masawayh and Bukhtishu ibn Jibril.
- **Abandoning bloodletting, purging and mercury (end of humoral medicine)** [`bloodletting_harm`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bloodletting_harm.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Venesection (fasd) and cupping (hijama) are routine, recommended in prophetic tradition and in Galen alike; barbers cup in the markets, court physicians bleed the caliph by the calendar and the stars. Questioning it attacks both religion and medicine. Local: cuppers and barbers in the Karkh markets; Yuhanna ibn Masawayh; Salmawayh ibn Bunan.
- **Counting and mapping cases to find causes (epidemiology)** [`epidemiology_mapping`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/epidemiology_mapping.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. The diwans survey land, count taxpayers and pay rolls of soldiers by name, but nobody records deaths or causes. The method exists; the question does not. Mosque imams and washers of the dead know who died where. Local: diwan al-kharaj (land tax office) and diwan al-jund (army pay rolls); washers of the dead and gravediggers at the cemeteries of Quraysh and Bab al-Harb.
- **Hand washing with soap** [`hand_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hand_hygiene.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept high. Ritual ablution (wudu') before each of five daily prayers makes hand and face washing a habit of every Muslim; hands are washed before and after meals, often with ushnan (saltwort ash). Nobody links hands to fever, and physicians and midwives do not wash between patients. Local: ablution basins at the Friday mosques; ushnan sellers.
- **Boiling drinking water and protecting wells** [`boiled_water`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/boiled_water.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Galenic and Hippocratic texts rank waters and advise boiling bad ones; the rich cool water in porous jars and ice is carried to the palaces. Most people drink Tigris and canal water brought by water carriers. Fuel is dear in a city without forests. Local: water carriers (saqqa'un) drawing from the Tigris; Airs, Waters, Places in Syriac and early Arabic versions.
- **Slow sand filtration and chlorination of town water** [`water_filtration_chlorination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_filtration_chlorination.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Water from the Tigris and the canals from the Euphrates is muddy; households let it settle in large unglazed jars, which also cool it by sweating. Sand filter beds are buildable by canal engineers; chlorination is out of reach. Local: Nahr Isa and the Sarat canal; potters of porous water jars.
- **Latrines and sewers (keeping excrement out of water, food and soil)** [`sanitation_sewerage`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sanitation_sewerage.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Islamic purity law is strict about excrement and urine, and houses have latrines over cesspits; the better quarters have covered drains to the canals. Waste still ends in the canals and the Tigris that the city drinks. Local: cesspit cleaners; jurists on purity (tahara).
- **Food hygiene (cooking, flies, carriers)** [`food_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_hygiene.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept high. Ritual slaughter drains blood, pork and carrion are forbidden, and the market inspector (sahib al-suq or muhtasib) checks weights and spoiled goods. Flies, cooks' hands and carriers are no one's concern. Local: market inspector of Karkh; cookshops and harisa sellers.
- **Quarantine and isolation of the sick** [`quarantine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quarantine.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. A saying of the Prophet orders that one should not enter a land where plague (ta'un) is, nor flee from it, and Umar is said to have turned back from plague-struck Syria in 639. It is read as trust in God rather than isolation, and the great plague waves ended in Iraq around 749. Local: hadith scholars; the story of Umar and the plague of Amwas.
- **Hospital hygiene and trained nursing** [`nursing_hospital_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nursing_hospital_hygiene.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Baghdad has a bimaristan from Harun al-Rashid's reign, probably founded by the Barmakid vizier Yahya ibn Khalid; the story of Jibril ibn Bukhtishu founding it is doubted. Physicians are salaried and the sick are fed, but there is no idea of cleaning between patients or separating fevers. Local: the bimaristan of Baghdad; Bukhtishu ibn Jibril; Gondeshapur in Khuzistan, the physicians' home tradition.
- **Cholera and typhoid spread through drinking water** [`cholera_waterborne`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cholera_waterborne.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Asiatic cholera stays in Bengal. Arabic hayda is any violent flux; dysentery and summer diarrhoea kill children every year in the hot months. Elsewhere: Bengal, where cholera is endemic.
- **Oral rehydration (water, salt and sugar)** [`oral_rehydration`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oral_rehydration.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Cane sugar from Khuzistan and salt are both in every market, and physicians already prescribe syrups (sharab) and barley water. The right proportions and the reason would be new. Local: sugar refiners of Khuzistan (Ahwaz, Tustar); druggists (attarun) of the Karkh market.
- **Plague carried by rats and fleas (and by coughing)** [`plague_vectors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/plague_vectors.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. The Justinianic plague returned to Iraq and Syria many times until about 749 and is remembered by name (ta'un). It has gone; rats and fleas are ordinary. The knowledge has no visible use here for five centuries.
- **Typhus carried by body lice (delousing)** [`typhus_lice`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typhus_lice.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Lice are ordinary among soldiers, prisoners and the poor. Camp fevers on the Byzantine frontier are blamed on bad air and fatigue. Washing and baking clothes is cheap; the reason would be new.
- **Malaria carried by mosquitoes (drainage, nets)** [`malaria_mosquito`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/malaria_mosquito.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Tertian and quartan fevers are well described by Galen and rife in the marshes of southern Iraq around Basra and Wasit, blamed on the air of stagnant water. People sleep on roofs and under nets against gnats, for comfort, not for fever. Local: the Batiha marshes between Wasit and Basra; al-Jahiz, a Basran with sharp eyes for insects.
- **Cinchona bark (quinine) against malaria** [`quinine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quinine.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept high. Cinchona grows only in the Andes. Fevers are treated with diet, bleeding, syrups and astrological timing. Elsewhere: Andean forests, source of cinchona bark.
- **Consumption (tuberculosis) is contagious** [`tuberculosis_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/tuberculosis_control.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept low. Consumption (sill) is known from the Greek books and blamed on ulcerated lungs and constitution; that it passes to those nearby is not discussed. Milk and sugar diets are prescribed.
- **Parasitic worms (hookworm, roundworm, tapeworm, guinea worm)** [`parasitic_worms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/parasitic_worms.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Physicians distinguish long, round and small worms (Greek tradition) and think they breed from corrupt humours. Remedies like pomegranate root and male fern work. The guinea worm (al-irq al-madani) is known from Hijaz; transmission by water and soil is unknown.
- **Fresh food prevents scurvy (citrus, vitamin C)** [`scurvy_citrus`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scurvy_citrus.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Rare on land; Indian Ocean voyages hop between ports and seldom run long enough. The citron (utrujj) is grown, while the sour orange and lemon only become common in Iraq in the following century. Dates and fresh greens protect most people. Elsewhere: India, home of the sour orange and lemon.
- **Deficiency diseases (beriberi, rickets, pellagra, goitre, night blindness)** [`vitamins_deficiency`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vitamins_deficiency.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Liver for night blindness is in the Greek books. Disease is excess, blockage or bad air, never a missing substance. The poor of Baghdad live on bread and dates and suffer in famine years.
- **Variolation (inoculation with smallpox matter)** [`variolation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/variolation.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Smallpox (judari) and measles (hasba) are known childhood killers, but no one inoculates. Material exists in every outbreak; the idea of deliberately giving a mild case would horrify physicians and jurists alike.
- **Smallpox vaccination with cowpox** [`smallpox_vaccination`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/smallpox_vaccination.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Smallpox is present, but cowpox is not known or looked for; the dairy herds of the Sawad are water buffalo, cattle, sheep and goats.

- **Wound care (stop bleeding, clean, tie vessels, leave dirty wounds open)** [`wound_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wound_care.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Surgeons (jarrahun) suture, splint, cauterise and dress wounds with wine, vinegar, oils and honey after Galen and Paul of Aegina, known through Syriac. Cautery (kayy) is the great remedy. The armies on the Byzantine frontier take physicians, never enough. Local: jarrahun attached to the caliph's army; Bukhtishu ibn Jibril.
- **Antiseptics (strong spirit, chlorinated lime, carbolic acid, iodine)** [`antiseptics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/antiseptics.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Wine, vinegar and honey on wounds and boiling oil or cautery are used for other reasons. Strong spirit is not yet made in quantity; pitch, alum and vitriol are at hand.
- **Sterilising instruments and dressings by heat** [`heat_sterilisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heat_sterilisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Cautery irons are heated for burning, not for cleanliness. Instruments are wiped and reused; pus is expected and called laudable.
- **Safe childbirth (clean hands, patience, cord care, forceps)** [`childbirth_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/childbirth_care.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Midwives (qawabil) deliver on birthing stools; male physicians give advice from Galen and Soranus but rarely attend. No forceps. Childbed fever is common and blamed on retained humours. Local: midwives of the harem and the city quarters.
- **First aid and resuscitation** [`first_aid_resuscitation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/first_aid_resuscitation.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Bleeding is stopped by pressure, cautery and styptics; drowning victims are turned and shaken. Chest compression and mouth-to-mouth breathing are unknown.
- **Ether anaesthesia** [`ether_anaesthesia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ether_anaesthesia.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept medium. Surgeons dull pain with opium, henbane and mandrake, risky and uneven. Ether needs strong sulphuric acid and strong spirit, neither made here.
- **Pain relief with opium and willow bark (laudanum, morphine, aspirin)** [`opium_analgesia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/opium_analgesia.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Opium (afyun) is a staple of the druggists, known from Dioscorides and Galen and compounded into theriac (tiryaq), which the caliph's physicians prepare with ceremony. Doses are by eye; overdose is known to kill. Willow is used for fever in Dioscorides. Local: Yuhanna ibn Masawayh, a compounder of drugs; theriac makers of the court.
- **Blood groups and transfusion** [`blood_groups_transfusion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blood_groups_transfusion.md) — K0, use none, make impossible, accept low
- **Human anatomy from dissection** [`anatomy_dissection`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/anatomy_dissection.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Anatomy is Galen's, read in Syriac and early Arabic summaries. Human dissection is unthinkable to jurists. Yuhanna ibn Masawayh is later reported to dissect apes, one sent from Nubia to the court in 836. Local: Yuhanna ibn Masawayh; Hunayn ibn Ishaq, a young man hunting for Greek copies of Galen.
- **Circulation of the blood** [`blood_circulation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/blood_circulation.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Galen's model rules. Venous blood is made in the liver and consumed by the body, some seeps through invisible pores in the heart's septum, and the arteries carry vital spirit. A ligature on an arm would already show the flow.
- **Physical diagnosis (percussion, stethoscope, thermometer, pulse count)** [`clinical_thermometer_stethoscope`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/clinical_thermometer_stethoscope.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Physicians take the pulse after Galen's many kinds and inspect urine in a flask (tafsira). Temperature is judged by hand and nobody counts beats against a clock; a pulse watch is the water clock.
- **Tooth decay and dental care** [`dental_care`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/dental_care.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. The miswak chewing stick (arak twig) is used several times a day as prophetic practice. Tooth worms are blamed for decay; sugar is a luxury of the rich, and their teeth show it. Extraction is the barber's job. Local: miswak sellers at the mosque gates.
